text:
Predicates:
ListedInYelp(x) ::: x is listed in Yelp's recommendations.
HasRatingGreaterThanFour(x) ::: x has a rating greater than four.
ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(x) ::: x receives many negative reviews.
ProvidesTakeOut(x) ::: x provides take-out service.
PopularAmongLocals(x) ::: x is popular among local residents.
Store(x) ::: x is a store.

Premises:
∀x (ListedInYelp(x) → ¬ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(x)) ::: If a restaurant is listed in Yelp's recommendations, then it has not received many negative reviews.
∀x (HasRatingGreaterThanFour(x) → ListedInYelp(x)) ::: All restaurants with a rating greater than four are listed in Yelp's recommendations.
∃x (¬ProvidesTakeOut(x) ∧ ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(x)) ::: Some restaurants that do not provide take-out service receive many negative reviews.
∀x (PopularAmongLocals(x) → HasRatingGreaterThanFour(x)) ::: All restaurants that are popular among local residents have ratings greater than four.
Store(hamdenSubway) ∧ (HasRatingGreaterThanFour(hamdenSubway) ∨ PopularAmongLocals(hamdenSubway)) ::: The Hamden Plaza Subway store has a rating greater than four, or it is popular among local residents.

Conclusion:
(ProvidesTakeOut(hamdenSubway) ∧ ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(hamdenSubway)) → (HasRatingGreaterThanFour(hamdenSubway) ∧ ¬ProvidesTakeOut(hamdenSubway)))
